newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ally of France's Juppe comes out for party rival.
newsitem.headline: Ally of France's Juppe comes out for party rival.

text.p: The closest ally of ex-prime minister Alain Juppe on Monday appeared to bow to intense pressure to oust Juppe from the leadership of France's Gaullist RPR party in the wake of its election defeat.
Former interior minister Jean-Louis Debre seemed to endorse a bid for the leadership of the Rally for the Republic (RPR) by former National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin.
"Philippe Seguin may be the one to spread the voice of modernity and of the renewal of the Gaullist movement," Debre told LCI television.

Juppe, the RPR president, appointed Debre as his deputy in a bid to retain the party's reins in the face of an onslaught from his opponents following the right's disastrous defeat in the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.
Seguin, who took over as the right's campaign leader between the two rounds of voting, has made a formal bid for the leadership of the party founded by President Jacques Chirac.
The RPR leadership is to meet on Wednesday to set the date for an emergency congress to name its president.

Juppe has not said whether he would stand for re-election as party leader in the emergency congress. His opponents have declared unacceptable his bid to hold the congress in September, and Debre last week endorsed demands that it be held next month.
